resources.string: Each control is sent to Android and then read back. A switch records what you asked for; the line under it is what this device actually confirmed.
Debugging, installation, network and device restrictions
Pilot — debugging stays available unless you turn it off
Production — debugging is off unless you turn it on
Requested, but this device did not confirm it
Not available on this Android version
No verification has run on this device yet.
Saved. Nothing changes on the device until you apply and verify.
Protection is paused, so these choices are recorded but not enforced. They are applied when protection is activated again.
System policy was applied and verified on this device.
This device did not confirm every requested control: %1$s
The administrator session expired. Enter the PIN again to change system policy.
The restriction is withdrawn the next time policy is applied, and the capability becomes available to whoever is holding this device.

Turns off developer options and ADB. USB debugging is the documented way to recover a device whose management app cannot be reached, so switching this on removes the current recovery path. Do not enable it before a signed update has been installed successfully on this hardware.
The device still charges over USB, but it cannot be mounted as storage, so files cannot be copied on or off with a cable.
Applications can no longer be installed from a file or from any source outside an approved installer. On Android 10 and later the block also covers other profiles on the device.

Blocks every installer on the device. Android applies this to the management app as well, so Device Guard cannot install its own signed updates while this is on. Leave it off until updates are delivered another way.
No account can be added, removed or reconfigured in Settings, including an account an installed application needs in order to sign in.
Whoever is using the device cannot create or edit a VPN. A VPN already configured by management keeps working.
The Settings action that clears Wi-Fi, mobile data and Bluetooth settings at once becomes unavailable, so management connectivity cannot be dropped by accident.
The device cannot share its connection with other devices over Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth.

Whoever is using the device cannot add or change Wi-Fi networks. What a given manufacturer actually refuses varies, so this control is reported on its own and never marks protection as faulty by itself. If the device also loses the network it is managed over, only on-site access can restore it.
The private DNS mode cannot be changed, so name resolution cannot be pointed at an unfiltered resolver. Requires Android 10 or later.
The clock cannot be set by hand. Certificate checks and scheduled tasks depend on it. Requires Android 9 or later.
The device cannot be restarted into Safe Boot, which would otherwise start it with the management policy inactive.
The reset action in Settings becomes unavailable. A reset started from the hardware recovery menu is outside what any management application can block.
No new user or work profile can be created, and on Android 9 and later switching users is blocked as well. This prevents a second, unmanaged session on the same device.
Applications cannot be removed from the device by the person using it.
Force stop, clear data and clear cache become unavailable in Settings, so a managed application cannot be neutralised by clearing its state.
System policy controls were applied and verified
